answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the hollow schedule in the zenith ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the plume checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 219 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 3 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 15 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
